bullets.text: 10-year Treasury at 4.95%, +4 bp on the day. This is the single biggest input to your rate.
Published 30-year survey at 7.24%, -8 bp week over week. It is a weekly average and always lags your rate sheet.
Mortgage spread 226 bp, normal at the 62th percentile of 10 years. That is 2.26 points of the 7.24% rate coming from spread, not from Treasuries.
Core CPI +0.34% (2026-09 reference month), the newest inflation read the market has.

why.headline: Mortgage rates are under upward pressure. The 10-year Treasury is 4.95% (+4 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.21%.
why.summary: The 10-year Treasury is at 4.95%, +4 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved -8 bp. That breaks down exactly: +2 bp from Treasuries and -10 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 226 bp, which is normal and sits at the 62th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 18 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.

contributions.label: Core CPI
contributions.chain: Core CPI → ↑ Inflation expectations → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Realised core inflation is the largest single input to forward inflation pricing.
The 10Y is a real yield plus an inflation expectation. Expectations move the nominal.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

brief.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
brief.body: Mortgage rates: 7.24% published 2026-10-29, modeled 7.21% today. 10-year Treasury: 4.95% (+4 bp). MBS: -5.60 ticks. Rate bias: Worsening. The mortgage spread is 226 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: FOMC Rate Decision on 11-04, Nonfarm Payrolls on 11-06. Biggest risk: FOMC Rate Decision. A hot print reverses any Treasury rally. What LOs should know: no action. Rates are inside the daily noise band
